questions.q: Distinguish between the political executive and the permanent executive.
answer: In a democracy the executive branch has two parts that work together but play different roles.

answer.text: This is made up of leaders elected by the people for a fixed term — the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers at the Centre. They take all the major policy decisions and are directly accountable to the people through elections and to Parliament.
This is made up of the civil servants, or bureaucracy, who are appointed on a long-term basis. They work under the political executive and carry out its decisions in the day-to-day administration.
In a democracy the political executive is more powerful, because those who are elected and answerable to the people must have the final say over appointed officials.

questions.q: Describe the three main institutions of government in India.
answer: Democracy in India works through three main institutions that share power and check one another.

answer.text: Parliament, made up of the Lok Sabha, the Rajya Sabha and the President, makes the laws, controls the budget and holds the executive accountable. Money bills can be introduced only in the directly elected Lok Sabha.
Headed by the Prime Minister, with the President as constitutional head, the executive runs the government and implements laws. The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.
An independent judiciary — the Supreme Court, High Courts and subordinate courts — interprets the Constitution, settles disputes, and through judicial review can strike down unconstitutional laws.
